sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Markdown to web page converter
sections.what: Reads the acceptance markdown and writes a styled HTML copy with headings, tables, code blocks and paragraphs. It then prints where the file was saved.
sections.why: Likely reason: a single downloadable page is easier to share and print than the markdown source. The script header states this purpose.
sections.watch_out: Tables end only when a line that does not start with a pipe appears, so a table directly followed by text without a blank line can run into that text.

summary: Turns a markdown acceptance report into one self-contained, styled HTML page that can be downloaded and printed.
purpose: Produces a readable HTML version of the research harness acceptance document for people who do not read markdown.
why: Likely reason: the report needs to be shared as a single file that opens in any web browser. The script header describes the output as a downloadable document.
how: Reads the markdown source line by line. Lines inside code fences become preformatted blocks. Lines starting with a pipe become table rows, and the separator row is skipped. Lines starting with hash marks become headings at the matching level. Other non-empty lines become paragraphs. All text is escaped first, then the page is written with its styling built in. The script prints the output path relative to the repository root.
inputs: The file docs/verification/research-harness-acceptance.md, found three folder levels above the script.
outputs: The file docs/verification/research-harness-acceptance.html, overwritten on each run, and one console line with its path.
risks: Only a small part of markdown is supported. Bold text, links and bullet lists appear as plain symbols. An unclosed code fence sends the rest of the document into a preformatted block. Reading and writing use the system default text encoding.
debug: If the output is missing, check that the markdown source exists at the expected path. If a table or code block looks wrong, look for a missing blank line or an unclosed code fence in the markdown. Plain-looking bullet points are expected, not a bug.
